claims.text: Compositional tuning can create a thermal-conductivity gradient across the thickness of an HEA intermediate layer.
A compositionally induced thermal-conductivity gradient can improve heat-transfer capability while preserving structural integrity under plasma-facing reactor conditions.
Uniform-composition HEAs are currently used as intermediate materials in plasma-facing reactor components.
The proposed effect should hold over 500–1500°C.
The proposed effect should hold under mechanical loading typical of plasma-facing reactor environments.
The compositional gradient produces a gradient in atomic-scale bonding within the HEA layer.
The compositional gradient produces a gradient in lattice parameters within the HEA layer.
The compositional gradient creates regions having different thermal conductivities.
Regions with different thermal conductivities enable more efficient heat dissipation.
The graded HEA retains the alloy's mechanical strength.
The graded HEA retains resistance to thermal stress.
The graded HEA will transfer heat better than a uniform-composition HEA intermediate layer.
The graded HEA will show no significant degradation of structural integrity under the specified conditions.
The hypothesis is expected to apply when the compositional gradient does not exceed constituent-element solubility limits.
The hypothesis is expected to apply when the HEA maintains phase stability under reactor conditions.
